options: Actively maintain perioperative normothermia, generally targeting at least about 36°C unless patient-specific factors dictate otherwise
Accept mild hypothermia because it reduces SSI risk
Temperature management has no relationship to perioperative outcomes
questions.explanation: A core temperature of 35.7 degrees C is perioperative hypothermia. Active warming and temperature monitoring are used to maintain normothermia, commonly around or above 36 degrees C, because hypothermia is associated with adverse outcomes including impaired coagulation, delayed drug metabolism, discomfort, and in some settings increased SSI risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A diabetic patient's intraoperative glucose is 228 mg/dL. Which SSI-prevention target has been exceeded?
questions.explanation: A glucose of 228 mg/dL exceeds the commonly used perioperative target of less than 180 mg/dL in many surgical patients. Hyperglycemia is associated with infection and other complications, while overly aggressive treatment that causes hypoglycemia is also harmful.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects the role of supplemental inspired oxygen in SSI prevention?
options: Adequate oxygenation is important, but a high FiO2 should be individualized rather than treated as a universal SSI-prevention requirement
Every surgical patient should receive FiO2 above 0.8 solely to prevent SSI
FiO2 below 0.3 is required to prevent SSI
Inspired oxygen concentration has no physiologic relevance
questions.explanation: Adequate tissue oxygenation is important for wound healing and host defense, but routine high inspired oxygen for every patient is not a universally accepted SSI-prevention requirement. FiO2 should meet oxygenation needs and applicable procedure-specific guidance while avoiding a rigid one-size-fits-all target.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A colectomy patient receives 6 L crystalloid and develops bowel edema. Which fluid-management principle was missed?
options: Maintain normovolemia rather than liberal fluid loading
questions.explanation: Large liberal crystalloid loads can cause interstitial and bowel edema without improving useful perfusion. Goal-directed maintenance of euvolemia seeks adequate organ and wound perfusion while avoiding both hypovolemia and unnecessary fluid overload.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which five measures are part of SSI-prevention strategy? (Select 5)
questions.explanation: SSI prevention is multifactorial: timely antimicrobial prophylaxis, normothermia, reasonable glycemic control, adequate oxygenation, and euvolemia each address different contributors to infection risk. The exact bundle should follow procedure- and patient-specific guidance.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Tracheal intubation of a patient with influenza generates fine droplets and droplet nuclei. How is the procedure classified for infection-control purposes?
questions.explanation: Tracheal intubation is treated as an aerosol-generating procedure in respiratory infection-control guidance because airway manipulation can disperse respiratory particles. Appropriate precautions depend on the pathogen and current transmission-based recommendations.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During an aerosol-generating airway procedure on a patient requiring airborne respiratory precautions, which FOUR PPE components are appropriate? (Select 4)
options: Shoe covers as the only additional protection
questions.explanation: When airborne respiratory precautions are indicated during an aerosol-generating airway procedure, protection includes gloves, gown, eye protection, and a fit-tested N95 or equivalent/higher-level respirator. A standard surgical mask does not provide equivalent respirator-level protection for that scenario.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which three procedures have evidence of higher respiratory-pathogen transmission risk? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Tracheal intubation, noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation, and manual ventilation around intubation have been associated with increased transmission risk in respiratory-outbreak literature. Risk depends on pathogen, technique, environment, and protective measures.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which four procedures are treated as aerosol-generating during respiratory-virus precautions? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Extubation, bronchoscopy, open airway suctioning, and high-flow nasal oxygen are commonly managed with aerosol precautions in respiratory-virus guidance. Classification can vary with pathogen and evolving evidence, so current institutional infection-control policy should guide practice.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which three procedures have less certain or unclear aerosol-transmission risk in the cited material? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Evidence for aerosol generation or transmission risk is less consistent for some activities such as chest compressions, nebulizer therapy, and nasogastric-tube insertion. Uncertainty should be distinguished from proof of no risk, and current pathogen-specific guidance should govern precautions.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA is about to extubate a patient with a respiratory infection. Which PPE strategy best reflects aerosol precautions?
options: Gloves, gown, eye protection, and appropriate respiratory protection
questions.explanation: Extubation involves airway manipulation and can provoke coughing and respiratory-particle dispersion. When aerosol precautions are indicated, gloves, gown, eye protection, and appropriate respirator-level protection should be in place before the procedure begins.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During upper GI endoscopy in a patient with a transmissible respiratory infection, which feature most increases concern for respiratory aerosol exposure?
options: Airway manipulation, coughing, gagging, or suctioning during the procedure
Passage of the endoscope through the GI tract alone guarantees aerosol transmission
Colonoscopy creates the same respiratory aerosol risk
questions.explanation: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy can provoke coughing, gagging, suctioning, or other airway manipulation that increases respiratory-particle exposure. Precautions should therefore reflect the specific respiratory pathogen, procedure details, ventilation, and current infection-control guidance rather than treating every endoscopy identically.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which surgical activity most clearly increases aerosol generation and therefore infection-control concern during an outbreak?
options: Use of high-speed devices such as drills
questions.explanation: High-speed drills, saws, and similar powered devices can generate aerosols or plumes from tissue and fluids. During an outbreak, that potential source-control problem warrants procedure- and pathogen-specific protective measures.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During failed intubation, a CRNA performs laryngoscopy competently but never verbalizes the backup plan, calls for help late, and fails to coordinate the team. Which performance domain is primarily deficient?
options: Non-technical cognitive, social, and personal skills
questions.explanation: Technical laryngoscopy skill alone does not ensure safe crisis performance. Failure to communicate the backup plan, call for help, and coordinate people reflects deficient nontechnical skills such as communication, teamwork, leadership, planning, and situational awareness.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which four items are non-technical skills central to crisis management? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Crisis nontechnical skills include situational awareness, decision-making, teamwork and leadership, and management of stress and fatigue. These cognitive and interpersonal capabilities complement procedural expertise and become especially important when workload is high.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which three functions do non-technical skills serve in crisis prevention and management? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Nontechnical skills help teams recognize deterioration early, communicate and coordinate effectively, and reduce preventable errors while interventions are organized. They improve how technical knowledge is deployed under pressure rather than replacing technical competence.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a code, the leader says, 'Epinephrine 1 mg IV,' and the nurse administers it but gives no verbal confirmation. Which CRM element is missing?
questions.explanation: Closed-loop communication requires the receiver to acknowledge the instruction and confirm completion so the sender knows the task was heard and executed correctly. Silent administration leaves the loop incomplete.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which two serious events have been associated with CRM communication failures? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Communication failures can contribute to retained objects, wrong-site procedures, medication errors, and other serious events. The cited examples demonstrate why standardized communication and verification are treated as safety defenses rather than optional etiquette.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a crisis, several clinicians begin duplicating the same tasks while other essential jobs are unattended. Which leader action best corrects the CRM failure?
options: Delay delegation until the diagnosis is certain
questions.explanation: When several people duplicate one task, the leader should explicitly assign roles so critical functions are covered without unnecessary overlap. Clear task ownership also makes it easier to identify when a job has not been completed.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During major hemorrhage, the CRNA anticipates the need for blood and calls for the rapid infuser before hypotension develops. Which CRM principle is most directly demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Calling for resources before overt collapse demonstrates perception of the evolving hemorrhage, comprehension of its significance, and anticipation of future need. That is situational awareness applied to resource management.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During malignant hyperthermia treatment, new information changes rapidly as temperature, ETCO2, and potassium evolve. The leader repeatedly gathers input and updates the treatment plan. Which CRM skill is being used?
questions.explanation: Dynamic decision-making means repeatedly updating decisions as new physiologic information arrives rather than rigidly following the initial plan. Seeking team input can improve the information available while the leader maintains clear direction.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During debrief, the team praises anticipation of hemorrhage, advance planning, and sustained attention to the patient. Which CRM element does this describe?
questions.explanation: In the cited CRM wheel, awareness includes anticipation, planning, and sustained attention. Recognizing a developing problem before decompensation and preparing resources in advance are practical expressions of that element.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During a code, the airway is stabilized but medication preparation becomes the team's limiting task. A CRNA leaves the airway role to assist with drugs after ensuring coverage. Which CRM capability is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Behavioral flexibility allows team members to change roles as the crisis evolves rather than clinging to an initial assignment. The transfer is safe only because airway coverage is deliberately maintained while the CRNA moves to the new limiting task.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During MH, the CRNA calls for help and has a nurse read the crisis checklist aloud. Which CRM element is most directly represented?
options: Communication using cognitive aids and early help
questions.explanation: Calling for help early and using an emergency manual are both communication-support behaviors in the cited CRM framework. The cognitive aid externalizes memory so the team can communicate and execute required steps under high workload.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During massive hemorrhage, the CRNA identifies the highest-priority tasks and delegates blood, lines, and labs. Which CRM element is most directly demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Dynamic prioritization identifies which tasks are most urgent, while workload distribution assigns them to available team members. During hemorrhage, delegating blood, vascular access, and laboratory work prevents one clinician from becoming the bottleneck.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a near miss, the team analyzes both its decisions and how the room setup contributed. Which CRM element does this represent?
questions.explanation: Evaluation after an event examines decisions, errors, near misses, and environmental contributors so the team can learn rather than simply assign blame. This converts experience into 'error wisdom' and system improvement.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During unexpected hypoxemia, a CRNA assigns one person to obtain the airway cart and another to call for help. Which CRM element is best represented?
questions.explanation: Obtaining equipment and summoning help are simultaneous high-priority tasks. Explicitly distributing them across team members demonstrates workload allocation within dynamic prioritization.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA calls for help early during unexpected hypoxemia. Which CRM behavior is most directly demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Early help-seeking is a core crisis communication behavior because it expands available expertise and resources before the situation becomes unrecoverable. Waiting until collapse can turn a manageable problem into a resource-limited emergency.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a near miss, the team reconstructs its decisions, identifies why the error nearly reached the patient, and changes its future response. Which CRM element is most directly demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Reconstructing how a near miss developed and changing future behavior demonstrates evaluation and learning from error. The goal is to understand why defenses nearly failed and strengthen future performance rather than celebrate that no harm occurred.
questions.topic: Crisis resource management and non-technical skills
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During hypotension, a CRNA keeps treating presumed propofol vasodilation while ignoring rising airway pressures and unilateral breath sounds. Which cognitive error best fits?
questions.explanation: Fixation occurs when attention remains locked on an initial explanation despite discordant new evidence. Rising airway pressures and unilateral breath sounds should force reconsideration of presumed anesthetic vasodilation and broaden the differential.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA insists hypotension must be anesthetic-related and ignores accumulating evidence of hemorrhage. Which fixation subtype is this?
options: Cognitive tunnel vision: 'this and only this'
questions.explanation: The 'this and only this' fixation pattern is cognitive tunnel vision: one diagnosis dominates interpretation and contradictory data are discounted. A deliberate diagnostic pause and alternative differential can break the fixation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA dismisses anaphylaxis solely because it is uncommon despite compatible findings. Which fixation subtype is this?
questions.explanation: Avoidance fixation rejects an important diagnosis because it seems unlikely or undesirable rather than because the evidence excludes it. Low base rate does not justify dismissing anaphylaxis when the clinical pattern is compatible.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA assumes an abnormal blood pressure is just cuff artifact without adequately reassessing the patient. Which fixation subtype is this?
questions.explanation: Artifact fixation assumes an abnormal value is equipment error or otherwise benign without adequately checking the patient and measurement system. Suspected artifact should be verified, not used as a reason to stop assessment.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which three strategies can reduce fixation errors during crises? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Cognitive aids externalize key steps, mental breaks can interrupt tunnel vision, and simulation builds recognition of fixation and team challenge behaviors. Each creates an opportunity to reconsider an incorrect mental model.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During malignant hyperthermia, cognitive load is high and the team risks omitting treatment steps. A nurse reads the emergency manual aloud while actions are completed. What safety tool is being used?
questions.explanation: A cognitive aid is an external memory and decision-support tool used to reduce omission during high-stress events. Having one person read the emergency manual while others perform actions is often more reliable than expecting the entire team to recall every step.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which five resources are examples of cognitive aids? (Select 5)
questions.explanation: Emergency manuals, checklists, crisis-cart instructions, airway algorithms, and resuscitation reference cards all externalize critical information. They are cognitive aids because they support memory and sequencing when stress and workload impair recall.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which three benefits do cognitive aids provide during crises? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Cognitive aids can reduce omitted steps, standardize response, and decrease reliance on memory during rare crises. Their benefit depends on accessibility, team familiarity, and integration into actual workflow.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During malignant hyperthermia, the team uses the stepwise instructions attached to the MH cart rather than relying on memory alone. Which safety strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Stepwise MH-cart instructions are a cognitive aid because they organize treatment and reduce memory burden during a rare, rapidly evolving emergency. The aid supplements clinical judgment and team leadership rather than replacing them.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After two failed intubation attempts, the team follows a difficult-airway algorithm to determine the next step and avoid repeated ineffective attempts. What type of tool is guiding the response?
questions.explanation: A difficult-airway algorithm is a cognitive aid that structures escalation after failed attempts and helps prevent repeated ineffective actions. It supports timely transition to alternative oxygenation and airway strategies.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which cognitive aid is specifically designed to support the pre-incision safety time-out?
questions.explanation: The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist structures key checks around surgery, including the pre-incision team time-out. It is a cognitive and communication aid intended to ensure critical information is actively confirmed rather than assumed.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a wrong-drug event, the department adds distinct labels and barcode scanning. Which response best reflects modern safety science?
questions.explanation: Changing labeling and adding barcode verification modifies the system that allowed the wrong-drug event to occur. This systems-focused response creates stronger defenses than relying only on telling individuals to 'be more careful.'
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a wrong-site block, the review examines site marking, time-out reliability, and staffing rather than blaming one person. Which approach is this?
options: Continuous quality improvement focused on systems
questions.explanation: Continuous quality improvement asks how processes, staffing, verification, environment, and other system conditions contributed to the event. A wrong-site block is therefore reviewed across multiple defenses rather than reduced to individual blame.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After wrong-site surgery, the final clinician action is obvious, but several verification defenses also failed. What should the quality review prioritize?
options: Processes and system conditions that allowed multiple defenses to fail
Punishment of the final clinician only
Only the last action before incision
questions.explanation: The review should identify why independent defenses such as site marking, verification, and time-out processes all failed or were bypassed. Strengthening those system layers reduces recurrence more reliably than focusing only on the last person in the chain.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA discovers a double dose of ondansetron was given but no harm occurred. What obligation remains?
options: Disclose the error according to policy
Say nothing because there was no harm
Alter the chart to show the intended dose
questions.explanation: A medication error can warrant transparent disclosure even when no injury results, depending on its clinical significance and institutional requirements. Disclosure should accurately explain what occurred, known effects, and follow-up without minimizing or speculating.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Postoperative delirium goes unrecognized for a day because no one identifies the diagnosis. Which error category best fits?
options: Diagnostic error due to delayed recognition
questions.explanation: Failure to recognize postoperative delirium in a timely manner is a diagnostic error because the primary failure is delayed identification of the condition. Contributing communication or monitoring failures can coexist and should also be examined.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: PACU is told the patient received morphine when hydromorphone was actually given, leading to overdose. Which error type best captures the primary failure?
questions.explanation: The receiving team was given incorrect medication information, so the primary failure occurred during transfer of information. A systems review should also examine medication reconciliation and verification defenses that might have caught the discrepancy before additional dosing.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital eliminates routine anesthesia-machine maintenance to save money and a vaporizer later fails. Which error category best fits?
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance is a system defense intended to identify equipment deterioration before patient care is affected. Eliminating it removes a preventive safeguard and allows a foreseeable equipment failure to reach the clinical environment.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A new evidence-based ERAS protocol improves multimodal analgesia and recovery. Which IOM quality domain is most directly supported?
questions.explanation: An evidence-based ERAS protocol applies interventions supported by current evidence to improve recovery. That most directly advances effectiveness, although successful implementation may also improve safety, efficiency, and patient-centered outcomes.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital compares antiemetic use by insurance status to identify treatment gaps. Which quality domain is it primarily assessing?
questions.explanation: Comparing treatment by insurance status asks whether clinically similar patients receive comparable care despite a socioeconomic characteristic. That is fundamentally an equity measurement, provided the analysis appropriately adjusts for relevant clinical differences.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department staffs in-house anesthesia to reduce delays for emergency cesarean delivery. Which quality domain is most directly improved?
questions.explanation: Timeliness means reducing harmful waits and delays. In-house staffing that shortens response time for emergency cesarean delivery primarily improves timely access to needed anesthesia care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA modifies the anesthetic plan after discussing and respecting a patient's religious beliefs. Which quality domain is most directly reflected?
questions.explanation: Patient-centered care incorporates individual values, beliefs, preferences, and needs into clinically appropriate planning. Discussing religious considerations and adapting the anesthetic when safely possible directly reflects that domain.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital bundle lowers postoperative infection rates. Which NHQDR core area is most directly improved?
questions.explanation: Healthcare-associated and postoperative infections are preventable harms targeted by patient-safety programs. A bundle that lowers infection rates therefore most directly improves the patient-safety domain.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An interdisciplinary team uses one shared plan across multiple units for a complex patient. Which NHQDR core area does this best represent?
questions.explanation: Care coordination integrates plans and information across clinicians, services, and settings. A shared interdisciplinary plan reduces fragmentation and conflicting treatment as the patient moves among units.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A clinic provides smoking-cessation classes before elective surgery. Which NHQDR core area is most directly addressed?
questions.explanation: Smoking cessation is preventive health promotion that reduces future disease and perioperative risk rather than treating a current surgical complication. It therefore fits the healthy-living domain.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital program reduces patients' out-of-pocket surgical expenses. Which NHQDR core area is most directly improved?
questions.explanation: Reducing out-of-pocket expense directly improves affordability, a major determinant of whether patients can obtain and sustain needed care. Lower cost can also improve access, but the stated intervention most directly targets financial burden.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An audit finds that Black patients undergoing comparable cesarean deliveries receive general anesthesia more often than White patients even after clinically relevant differences are considered. What concern should the team investigate?
options: A potential disparity in anesthetic technique and access to neuraxial care
General anesthesia is inherently the preferred technique for Black patients
Race itself determines the safest anesthetic
The pattern cannot represent an equity issue
questions.explanation: A persistent technique difference after accounting for clinically relevant factors warrants investigation for disparity, but the audit should examine urgency, contraindications, patient preference, labor neuraxial access, institutional pathways, and potential bias before attributing causation. Race itself should not be treated as a biologic explanation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A Hispanic adolescent needs mental-health treatment but cannot access it. Which cited 2023 disparity does this reflect?
options: Limited access to adolescent mental-health care
questions.explanation: The cited 2023 material identifies limited mental-health treatment access among adolescents, with particular barriers reported for low-income and Hispanic youth. The scenario reflects an access disparity, not a difference in whether mental-health illness deserves treatment.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An appropriate kidney-transplant candidate faces major barriers to transplant evaluation and listing. Which health-equity issue does this illustrate?
options: Dialysis has eliminated the need for transplantation
Transplant access is uniform across eligible populations
Kidney failure does not create long-term access issues
questions.explanation: For appropriate candidates, transplantation can provide major survival and quality-of-life benefits, yet referral, evaluation, listing, organ availability, geography, socioeconomic factors, and structural barriers can produce unequal access. Equity analysis focuses on those modifiable pathway differences.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A clinician gives less opioid to a Black patient with the same fracture severity because of a belief that Black patients tolerate pain better. What does this represent?
options: False race-based beliefs contributing to pain disparities
questions.explanation: The decision uses a false race-based assumption rather than the individual patient's pain, injury, physiology, and treatment response. Such beliefs can contribute to systematic undertreatment and are not a valid biologic basis for analgesic dosing.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with sickle-cell disease lacks coordinated chronic-pain care. Which ASA equity priority is most directly relevant?
questions.explanation: Fragmented sickle-cell pain care is directly relevant to equitable access to effective pain management. Coordinated disease-specific services can improve continuity and reduce reliance on episodic crisis-only treatment.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A child from a minority background receives less analgesia for severe ED pain than a clinically similar child. Which equity priority is most directly implicated?
questions.explanation: A systematic difference in analgesia for clinically comparable children is a pediatric equity concern. The appropriate response is to examine assessment, prescribing, communication, access, and clinician or system bias rather than assume different analgesic need from race or ethnicity.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An uninsured patient delays needed surgery until the condition becomes an emergency. Which ASA equity priority is most directly implicated?
questions.explanation: Lack of insurance can delay preventive, diagnostic, and definitive treatment until disease becomes more severe or emergent. The scenario therefore most directly concerns access to insurance as an upstream barrier, while recognizing that insurance alone does not guarantee timely access.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An hourly worker without paid sick leave repeatedly misses preoperative testing. Which access barrier is most directly responsible?
questions.explanation: Without paid sick leave, attending preoperative testing can mean losing wages or employment security. That economic constraint directly interferes with healthcare access even when testing itself is available.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient avoids recommended care because prior discrimination created deep distrust of the healthcare system. Which access barrier does this illustrate?
options: Long-standing distrust of the healthcare system
questions.explanation: Prior discrimination can produce durable distrust that reduces willingness to seek or remain engaged in care. Addressing the barrier requires respectful communication, transparency, and reliable care rather than labeling the patient's reluctance as noncompliance.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital mandates health-equity training, changes policy, and measures compliance across every perioperative department. At which APSF intervention level is this primarily operating?
questions.explanation: Mandatory training, policy change, and organization-wide measurement alter the environment across departments rather than relying on isolated individual behavior. Those are system-level equity interventions.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Outside required institutional programs, a CRNA independently participates in community outreach intended to reduce local health disparities. At which APSF intervention level does this action primarily occur?
questions.explanation: When undertaken independently rather than as an institutional program, community outreach is an individual clinician action intended to understand or reduce local disparities. It can complement, but does not substitute for, system-level changes.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA independently pursues continuing education on disparities in anesthesia care. Which APSF intervention level is this?
questions.explanation: A clinician independently seeking education is acting at the individual level. The knowledge gained may influence practice, while organization-wide curricula, requirements, or accountability mechanisms would operate at the system level.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A hospital ties departmental bonuses to closing disparities in PONV prophylaxis. Which APSF intervention level is this?
questions.explanation: Departmental financial incentives are organizational levers designed to change behavior and outcomes across groups of clinicians. Linking them to measured disparity reduction therefore represents a system-level strategy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A quality project suspects a disparity in postoperative pain treatment. Which AANA-recommended action would allow the department to determine whether outcomes actually differ across racial and ethnic groups?
options: Issue an anti-discrimination statement without measurement
questions.explanation: A suspected disparity cannot be evaluated reliably without stratified outcome data. Collecting and analyzing clinically relevant outcomes by race, ethnicity, and other appropriate variables can reveal patterns that warrant deeper investigation while avoiding causal conclusions from raw differences alone.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA mentors a high-school student from an underrepresented group who is interested in healthcare. Which AANA recommendation does this support?
options: Encourage diverse students to consider nurse anesthesiology
questions.explanation: Mentoring students from underrepresented backgrounds can broaden awareness of nurse anesthesiology and support a more diverse future workforce. Recruitment efforts should expand opportunity without assuming any individual's interests or capabilities from demographic identity.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An audit finds PONV prophylaxis varies by clinician despite identical patient risk. Which AANA-recommended approach most directly reduces unwarranted variation?
options: Use an evidence-based standardized protocol when appropriate
questions.explanation: When patient risk is equivalent, an evidence-based standardized protocol can reduce clinician-dependent variation while preserving room for documented contraindications or individualized exceptions. Standardization therefore targets unwarranted, not clinically justified, variation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA considers local disease burden and access barriers when planning outreach. Which AANA recommendation is most directly applied?
questions.explanation: Effective outreach should reflect the actual disease burden, barriers, resources, and priorities of the community being served. Awareness of community needs helps avoid designing programs around clinician assumptions rather than local realities.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A competent adult refuses a regional block after risks, benefits, and alternatives are explained. What should the CRNA do?
options: Respect the refusal and offer alternatives
Ask the surgeon to override the decision
questions.explanation: A decisionally capable adult may refuse a recommended intervention after receiving relevant information and having questions answered. Respecting that informed refusal protects autonomy; the clinician should document the discussion and offer medically appropriate alternatives.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Hospital administrators pressure the anesthesia team to omit additional monitoring in a high-risk patient because of cost. The CRNA refuses because doing so would expose the patient to avoidable harm. Which ethical principle is most directly applied?
questions.explanation: Non-maleficence requires avoiding preventable harm. Cost stewardship matters, but omitting monitoring that is clinically indicated for a high-risk patient would allow a financial consideration to create avoidable safety risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA provides the same PONV prophylaxis to clinically similar patients regardless of insurance status. Which ethical principle is most directly reflected?
questions.explanation: Justice requires clinically comparable patients to receive equitable consideration regardless of insurance or social status. Applying the same risk-based PONV approach to similar patients demonstrates that principle.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA declines to place a block through infected skin because the procedure could cause harm. Which principle is most directly reflected?
questions.explanation: Placing a needle through infected tissue can increase the risk of spreading infection or causing deeper complications. Avoiding a procedure when its foreseeable harm outweighs benefit most directly reflects non-maleficence.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient requests a nerve block to reduce opioid use; after informed discussion, the CRNA agrees and performs it. Which two ethical principles are most directly involved?
questions.explanation: The patient's informed preference expresses autonomy, while performing an appropriate block expected to reduce opioid burden and improve recovery expresses beneficence. Ethical decisions often involve several principles simultaneously rather than a single isolated rule.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A qualified interpreter is used so a patient with limited English proficiency can meaningfully participate in anesthesia consent. Which principle is most directly supported?
questions.explanation: Meaningful autonomy depends on understanding. A qualified interpreter allows the patient to receive and question anesthesia information directly enough to make an informed choice, supporting valid consent rather than merely obtaining a signature.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient receives enough sedative to impair attention and recall, then is asked to sign anesthesia consent for a plan not previously discussed. What is the primary ethical concern?
options: Sedation may impair decision-making capacity, undermining valid consent
A signature alone guarantees valid consent
Sedation improves comprehension by reducing anxiety
The surgical consent automatically covers anesthesia
questions.explanation: Consent requires adequate decision-making capacity at the time of the decision. Sedation that impairs attention, comprehension, reasoning, or communication can undermine capacity, so substantive consent should ideally occur before such impairment when foreseeable.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A surgeon asks the CRNA to skip discussion of anesthesia-specific risks and alternatives to save time. Which response best protects valid informed consent?
options: Ensure the patient receives the anesthesia-specific information needed for informed consent before proceeding
Assume the surgeon's procedure consent automatically covers all anesthesia decisions
Wait until after surgery to discuss anesthesia risks
Obtain a signature without discussing material information
questions.explanation: Anesthesia-specific informed consent requires the patient to receive information relevant to the proposed anesthetic, including material risks, benefits, and alternatives as applicable. Who obtains or documents that consent depends on law and institutional policy; a surgical signature should not automatically be treated as anesthesia consent.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A competent patient refuses blood products for religious reasons. What does patient-centered care require?
options: Respect the patient's values and plan accordingly
Give blood if clinically indicated despite refusal
Refuse anesthesia unless blood is accepted
Ask the surgeon to override the refusal
questions.explanation: Patient-centered care integrates the individual's values into medically appropriate planning. A competent refusal of blood products should be respected, with acceptable alternatives and contingency plans discussed and documented before foreseeable bleeding whenever possible.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a patient reports intraoperative awareness, the anesthesia team acknowledges the experience, listens to the patient's concerns, and arranges appropriate psychological support. Which patient-centered-care dimension is most directly reflected?
questions.explanation: Acknowledging distress after awareness, listening without dismissing the report, and arranging psychological support address the emotional consequences of the experience. Appropriate clinical follow-up and documentation are also important, but the patient-centered dimension highlighted is emotional support.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: With the patient's permission, family members are included in preoperative discussion. Which patient-centered-care dimension does this reflect?
questions.explanation: With the patient's permission, involving family in discussion incorporates the patient's support system into care. Permission matters because family involvement should support, not displace, the patient's privacy and autonomy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: The anesthesia plan is coordinated with cardiology and nephrology for a complex patient. Which patient-centered-care dimension is most directly reflected?
questions.explanation: Coordinating cardiology, nephrology, and anesthesia recommendations reduces fragmented or conflicting plans for a complex patient. This most directly reflects coordination of care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient cannot travel easily, so telehealth preop is arranged. Which patient-centered-care dimension is most directly improved?
questions.explanation: Telehealth can reduce a transportation barrier by allowing appropriate preoperative assessment without travel. It therefore improves access when the patient's clinical needs and available technology make remote evaluation suitable.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient is transferred to the ICU with a detailed anesthesia handoff and clear next-step plan. Which patient-centered-care dimension is most directly reflected?
questions.explanation: A detailed ICU handoff transfers the anesthetic course, active problems, treatments, and next steps across a change in care setting. That preserves continuity and reduces information loss during transition.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient requests that her head covering remain in place for religious reasons whenever safely possible. Which patient-centered-care dimension is most directly reflected?
questions.explanation: Keeping a religious head covering in place whenever compatible with monitoring, sterility, and procedural safety incorporates the patient's values into care. Respect does not require ignoring genuine safety constraints; it requires seeking reasonable accommodation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA uses teach-back to verify understanding of postoperative instructions. Which patient-centered-care dimension is most directly reflected?
questions.explanation: Teach-back asks the patient to explain key instructions in their own words, allowing the clinician to identify misunderstanding and clarify it. This is stronger than asking only whether the patient understands.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA avoids assumptions and asks a patient directly about cultural preferences that may affect care. Which concept is being demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Asking the individual patient about preferences avoids stereotyping while making room for cultural values that may affect communication or care. Culturally responsive practice is individualized rather than based on assumptions about group membership.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient refuses recommended care because prior negative healthcare experiences destroyed trust. Which cultural-competence risk is illustrated?
options: Failure to seek or trust care
questions.explanation: Prior negative experiences can erode trust and lead patients to delay, avoid, or disengage from healthcare. Restoring trust requires respectful, transparent, reliable care rather than assuming reluctance reflects indifference to health.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A clinician misinterprets a patient's culturally influenced pain description and undertreats pain. Which risk of poor cultural competence is illustrated?
questions.explanation: If the clinician interprets a culturally influenced pain description through an inaccurate framework, communication failure can translate directly into undertreatment. Individual assessment and clarification are preferable to assumptions about how pain 'should' be expressed.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA completes structured training in cross-cultural communication. Which cultural-competence principle is being supported?
questions.explanation: Cross-cultural communication skills require continued learning because patient beliefs, identities, language needs, and clinician biases vary. Structured education supports competence, but cultural humility also requires ongoing self-reflection and individualized inquiry.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A study enrolls prisoners without additional safeguards. What is the primary research-ethics problem?
options: Prisoners are a vulnerable population requiring added protections
Prisoners may participate only in direct-benefit studies
Low-risk studies do not require consent
questions.explanation: Prisoners have specific additional federal protections because confinement can constrain voluntariness and create undue influence. Research involving prisoners must satisfy applicable regulatory criteria and review requirements rather than using ordinary enrollment procedures alone.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Researchers plan to enroll 15-year-olds without parental permission simply because the study is minimal risk. What is the problem?
options: Minors are a vulnerable population requiring additional protections
Minimal-risk research needs verbal consent only
questions.explanation: Children receive additional research protections, but the exact permission and assent requirements depend on the study, risk category, age, maturity, jurisdiction, and IRB determinations. Minimal risk does not by itself justify simply omitting all parental or guardian permission requirements.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A low-income participant is offered a payment so large relative to usual income that declining the study may no longer feel realistic. Which research protection is most threatened?
options: Voluntary participation free of undue influence
questions.explanation: An excessively influential payment can compromise voluntariness by making participation difficult to decline, particularly when it exploits financial vulnerability. The ethical concern is undue influence; coercion more specifically involves a threat of harm or penalty.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A researcher publishes identifiable patient data without permission. Which participant protection is directly violated?
questions.explanation: Publishing identifiable information without authorization can violate both privacy interests and the researcher's duty to maintain confidentiality. De-identification, consent terms, data-use rules, and applicable law determine what disclosure is permissible.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During emergence, loud music and conversation mask the pulse-oximeter alarm. Which distraction type is primarily responsible?
questions.explanation: Noise masks an auditory safety signal, so auditory distraction is the primary mechanism. Emergence is particularly vulnerable because multiple rapidly changing tasks compete for attention.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA checks email on a tablet and misses rising ETCO2. Which distraction type is most direct?
questions.explanation: Looking at email diverts the clinician's eyes from the patient and monitors, making visual distraction the immediate mechanism. The device may also impose cognitive distraction, but the missed ETCO2 trend follows diverted visual attention.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA charts, prepares a PCA, and troubleshoots equipment simultaneously. Which distraction mechanism is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Charting, medication preparation, and equipment troubleshooting all compete for working memory and task-switching capacity while patient monitoring continues. Excess cognitive load increases the chance of omission or delayed recognition.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During which three periods should OR noise be especially minimized? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Induction, emergence, and active crises are high-workload periods in which rapid physiologic changes and critical tasks require concentrated attention. Reducing nonessential noise protects communication and vigilance during those periods.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Team members repeatedly enter and leave during induction. Which distraction-control strategy is most appropriate?
options: Wait until after intubation to request quiet
questions.explanation: Repeated door openings and movement add visual, auditory, and workflow interruptions during a high-risk task. Controlling nonessential OR traffic reduces those distractions while preserving access for personnel needed for patient care.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: The team intentionally limits communication to essential safety-related discussion during a critical step. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: The sterile-OR concept temporarily limits conversation to information relevant to immediate patient care during critical tasks. It is analogous to a sterile-cockpit rule and should preserve, not suppress, essential safety communication.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After repeatedly silencing nuisance alarms during a long case, a CRNA becomes desensitized and fails to respond promptly to a true desaturation alarm. Which human-factors problem best explains the miss?
questions.explanation: Alarm fatigue develops when frequent nonactionable alarms reduce attention and urgency, increasing the chance that a true alarm will be missed or delayed. Better alarm configuration and response practices should reduce nuisance burden without disabling necessary protection.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During the surgical time-out, a CRNA continues charting without engaging. What is the best practice?
options: Stop and participate with full attention
Let the circulator complete it alone
Continue charting if the case is routine
questions.explanation: The time-out is an active team verification step, not background dialogue. Stopping competing work and participating allows each team member to hear, challenge, and confirm critical patient, procedure, site, and safety information.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA wants to use a personal phone during a stable portion of the case. Which principle should guide the decision?
options: Follow institutional policies on acceptable device use
Use the phone freely during maintenance
questions.explanation: Personal-device use should follow institutional policy and must never compromise vigilance, confidentiality, infection control, or response to patient needs. A physiologically stable moment does not eliminate the clinician's continuous monitoring responsibilities.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After a 16-hour shift, a CRNA is exhausted and cannot concentrate reliably. What is the safest response?
options: Recognize fatigue and seek relief to protect patient safety
questions.explanation: When fatigue degrades concentration enough to threaten safe performance, recognizing the impairment and obtaining relief or other appropriate mitigation protects the patient. Continuing solely because the shift is scheduled ignores a known human-performance hazard.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A fatigued CRNA has impaired memory and misses a medication dose. Which fatigue effect is illustrated?
questions.explanation: Memory lapse after prolonged wakefulness reflects fatigue-related cognitive impairment. Fatigue can degrade working memory, attention, calculation, judgment, and vigilance even when the clinician remains awake.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department finds errors cluster late in prolonged shifts. Which explanation best fits the pattern?
options: Errors cluster mainly at shift start
questions.explanation: Clustering of errors late in prolonged shifts is consistent with fatigue-related degradation in attention, reaction time, cognition, and decision-making. The pattern should prompt system-level review of scheduling and relief as well as individual countermeasures.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After severe sleep loss, a CRNA has slowed responses, poor concentration, and reduced awareness of the OR environment before induction. Which condition best explains this cluster?
questions.explanation: Slowed responses, poor concentration, and reduced situational awareness after major sleep loss are characteristic of clinically important fatigue. The safety issue is functional impairment, not simply the subjective feeling of being tired.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An immunocompromised patient is scheduled for surgery. Which link in the chain of infection is most clearly highlighted?
questions.explanation: Immunocompromise reduces the patient's ability to resist infection after exposure. That makes the patient the susceptible-host link and increases the importance of preventing transmission and protecting portals of entry.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A contaminated stethoscope remains colonized between patients and serves as a place where microorganisms persist before transfer. Which link in the chain of infection does it most directly represent?
questions.explanation: A reservoir is a place where an infectious agent can survive or persist before transmission. A contaminated reusable object can therefore function as a reservoir, while subsequent transfer from it represents the mode-of-transmission step.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with influenza coughs infectious respiratory material from the airway into the environment. Which chain-of-infection link does the coughing event represent?
questions.explanation: Coughing moves organisms from the infected respiratory tract into the environment. In the chain of infection, that route by which the agent leaves its reservoir or host is the portal of exit.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A central venous catheter breaches the skin and gives microorganisms direct access to the bloodstream. Which chain-of-infection link does the catheter site represent?
questions.explanation: An invasive catheter breaches the body's protective barrier and can provide microorganisms access to normally sterile tissue or bloodstream. The insertion site therefore functions as a portal of entry.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Hand hygiene before patient contact most directly interrupts which link in the chain of infection?
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene primarily interrupts transmission by removing or killing organisms before they move from one person, surface, or task to another. It is one of the most important defenses against contact-mediated spread.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA disinfects an IV stopcock before injecting medication. Which APSF infection-prevention strategy is being used?
options: Vascular access care with port disinfection
questions.explanation: Scrubbing an IV stopcock or needleless connector before access reduces inoculation of microorganisms into the vascular system. This is vascular-access infection prevention rather than a substitute for hand hygiene or aseptic medication preparation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient undergoes nasal antiseptic treatment before surgery. Which infection-prevention strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Nasal antisepsis aims to reduce the patient's microbial burden before surgery. It is a decolonization strategy and is often used selectively or as part of procedure-specific SSI-prevention bundles.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: The anesthesia workstation is disinfected thoroughly between cases. Which infection-prevention strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Cleaning high-touch anesthesia surfaces between patients reduces environmental bioburden and prevents the workstation from becoming a transmission source. Effective environmental cleaning complements hand hygiene and aseptic practice.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After touching the patient's mouth during intubation, a CRNA adjusts a clean vaporizer without changing gloves or cleaning hands. Which principle is violated?
options: Perform hand hygiene after airway contamination before touching clean zones
Hand hygiene is needed only after the case
Gloves remove the need for hand hygiene
The vaporizer is considered a dirty zone
questions.explanation: Airway manipulation contaminates gloves and hands with respiratory secretions. Moving directly from that dirty task to a clean vaporizer or medication area can transfer organisms, so appropriate glove removal and hand hygiene should occur before clean-zone contact.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A syringe cap falls to the floor; the CRNA picks it up and then continues working. What should occur before returning to clean tasks?
options: No action if gloves are worn
questions.explanation: A floor-contact item is contaminated and handling it creates a hand-hygiene indication before returning to clean patient-care or medication tasks. The dropped cap itself should not be reused simply because the clinician cleans their hands afterward.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA uses a cellphone and then begins medication preparation. What should happen first?
questions.explanation: Cellphones are high-touch personal objects that can become contaminated. Hands should be cleaned before medication preparation after phone use so organisms are not transferred into the clean medication workspace.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An anesthesia department audits hand-hygiene frequency during active care against the APSF recommendation cited in the course. Which minimum target should trigger compliance?
questions.explanation: The course cites an APSF process target of at least eight hand-hygiene events per hour during active anesthesia care. That numeric metric should not replace indication-based hygiene: every clinically indicated event still requires hand cleaning even if an hourly count has already been reached.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Immediately before urinary-catheter insertion, which WHO hand-hygiene moment applies?
options: Before a clean or aseptic procedure
questions.explanation: Urinary-catheter insertion is an aseptic procedure that introduces a device into a normally protected tract. WHO Moment 2 therefore requires hand hygiene immediately before the clean or aseptic task.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After suctioning oral secretions, which WHO hand-hygiene moment applies?
questions.explanation: Oral suctioning creates exposure to body fluids and respiratory secretions. WHO Moment 3 applies after the exposure risk, including after glove removal.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After adjusting bed rails without touching the patient, which WHO hand-hygiene moment applies?
questions.explanation: Bed rails are part of the patient's immediate environment and can carry organisms even without direct patient contact. WHO Moment 5 applies after touching patient surroundings.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: After taking a patient's pulse, which WHO hand-hygiene moment applies?
questions.explanation: Taking a pulse is direct patient contact, so WHO Moment 4 applies after the interaction. Hand hygiene helps prevent organisms acquired from that patient from being carried to subsequent surfaces or patients.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An infection limited to skin and subcutaneous tissue appears at the incision on postoperative day 10. Which SSI category is this?
questions.explanation: Superficial incisional SSI involves skin and subcutaneous tissue of the incision and must meet the applicable surveillance criteria within the defined period. Day 10 is compatible with the usual timing, but tissue depth and diagnostic criteria determine classification.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An infection involving fascia and muscle appears three weeks after surgery. Which SSI category best fits?
questions.explanation: Deep incisional SSI extends into deeper soft tissues such as fascia and muscle. Infection confined to skin or subcutaneous tissue would instead be superficial, while infection involving an operated organ or cavity would be organ/space.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: An intra-abdominal abscess forms 25 days after bowel surgery. Which SSI category best fits?
questions.explanation: An intra-abdominal abscess after bowel surgery involves an anatomic space manipulated during the operation rather than only the incision. That pattern fits organ/space SSI when the applicable surveillance criteria are met.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Why do healthcare facilities perform surgical-site infection surveillance?
options: To identify infection patterns, support prevention efforts, and evaluate quality improvement
Only to satisfy physician credentialing requirements
Because surveillance is solely the surgeon's responsibility
Because surveillance can replace infection-prevention practices
questions.explanation: SSI surveillance uses standardized definitions to detect trends, compare performance appropriately, and evaluate prevention interventions. Reporting and payment implications vary by procedure, surveillance program, jurisdiction, and payer, so surveillance should not be reduced to reimbursement alone.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which two consequences are commonly associated with surgical-site infections? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: SSIs commonly prolong hospitalization and contribute to readmission, reoperation, antimicrobial exposure, cost, and morbidity. The exact impact varies with infection depth, organism, procedure, and patient factors.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Cefazolin is completed 90 minutes before incision in an otherwise routine case. Why is this timing outside the usual prophylactic target?
options: Most prophylactic antibiotics should be administered within 60 minutes before incision
Cefazolin must be completed more than 90 minutes before incision
All prophylactic antibiotics use a 120-minute window
Prophylaxis should begin only after incision
questions.explanation: For cefazolin and most routine prophylactic antibiotics, administration is generally timed within 60 minutes before incision so effective tissue concentrations are present when contamination is most likely. Vancomycin and fluoroquinolones use a longer preincision window because infusion takes longer.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Vancomycin is started 100 minutes before incision. Which interpretation is correct?
options: The timing is appropriate because vancomycin may begin within a 120-minute window
It must start at least 3 hours before incision
questions.explanation: Starting vancomycin 100 minutes before incision falls within the commonly recommended 120-minute preincision window. The goal is to allow appropriate infusion while ensuring useful tissue concentrations by incision.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient's core temperature is 95.8°F (35.4°C) near the end of surgery. Which SSI-prevention goal has not been met?
questions.explanation: A core temperature of 35.4 degrees C is hypothermic and indicates failure to maintain perioperative normothermia. Active warming and temperature monitoring reduce hypothermia-related complications, with many perioperative pathways targeting approximately 36 degrees C or higher unless patient-specific circumstances dictate otherwise.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A diabetic patient's intraoperative glucose is 240 mg/dL. Which SSI-prevention target was not met?
questions.explanation: A glucose of 240 mg/dL exceeds the commonly used perioperative goal of less than 180 mg/dL for many surgical patients. Hyperglycemia is associated with infection and other adverse outcomes, while treatment must also avoid hypoglycemia.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Cefazolin was administered at incision for a spine fusion. At hour 5, the case is ongoing and the institutional redosing interval is 4 hours. Which action best maintains prophylactic tissue concentrations?
questions.explanation: When surgery continues beyond the antibiotic's recommended redosing interval, another dose helps maintain effective tissue concentrations. Major blood loss can also trigger earlier redosing depending on the drug and institutional protocol.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A colectomy ERAS pathway uses goal-directed fluid therapy. Which SSI-prevention principle does this support?
questions.explanation: Goal-directed fluid therapy attempts to maintain adequate circulating volume and perfusion while avoiding both hypovolemia and unnecessary fluid overload. That supports the normovolemia component of perioperative recovery and infection-prevention strategies.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A CRNA performs endotracheal intubation on a patient with suspected influenza. Which PPE approach is most appropriate when aerosol-generating-procedure precautions are indicated?
options: Gloves, gown, eye protection, and a fit-tested respirator or other recommended respiratory protection
A surgical mask and gloves only
questions.explanation: Intubation is an aerosol-generating airway procedure. When the suspected pathogen calls for airborne or AGP precautions, appropriate protection includes respirator-level respiratory protection plus eye protection, gown, and gloves according to current infection-control policy.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which procedure in a patient with active respiratory infection carries the higher aerosol-transmission risk?
questions.explanation: Tracheostomy insertion and airway suctioning directly manipulate the respiratory tract and can generate infectious aerosols. Outbreak literature has associated such airway procedures with higher transmission risk, making appropriate respiratory protection important.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Bag-mask ventilation before intubation in a patient with influenza is classified how for infection control?
questions.explanation: Manual bag-mask ventilation around intubation can disperse respiratory particles, particularly when mask seal is imperfect. It is therefore treated as a higher-risk aerosol-generating procedure in respiratory infection-control guidance.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A patient with influenza is placed on CPAP in PACU. How should this be treated for infection-control purposes?
options: As an aerosol-generating procedure with increased transmission risk
As a non-AGP because the system is closed
As a routine oxygen-delivery method without added precautions
questions.explanation: CPAP and other noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation can increase respiratory-particle dispersion and are commonly managed as aerosol-generating procedures when caring for transmissible respiratory infections.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: During resuscitation of a patient with respiratory infection, the team reviews procedures whose aerosol-transmission risk is less certain in the cited material. Which procedure belongs in that category?
questions.explanation: In the cited material, evidence linking defibrillation itself to aerosol transmission is uncertain. The surrounding resuscitation may include other clearly aerosol-generating activities, so PPE decisions should reflect the overall clinical scenario rather than defibrillation in isolation.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Open suctioning of airway secretions is classified as what?
questions.explanation: Open airway suctioning can expose clinicians to respiratory secretions and aerosolized particles and is commonly treated as an aerosol-generating procedure. Closed suction systems can reduce circuit opening but do not eliminate all transmission considerations.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: High-frequency oscillatory ventilation is classified as what?
questions.explanation: High-frequency oscillatory ventilation is categorized in the cited material among additional aerosol-generating procedures. Infection-control practice should follow current pathogen-specific guidance because classifications can evolve.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Adjustment of a noninvasive-ventilation mask is categorized how in the cited material?
questions.explanation: The cited material places noninvasive-ventilation mask adjustment in a less-certain aerosol-risk category. Uncertain evidence does not mean no risk, particularly because mask manipulation can create leaks around positive-pressure support.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Nebulized albuterol in PACU is categorized how in the cited material?
questions.explanation: Nebulizer therapy has had variable classification because the generated aerosol may arise from medication solution rather than directly from patient respiratory fluid, while patient coughing can still disperse infectious particles. The cited course material therefore appropriately labels transmission risk as uncertain.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Disconnecting a ventilator circuit for a circuit change in a patient with influenza is categorized how?
questions.explanation: Ventilator disconnection can release circuit contents and respiratory particles into the environment. The cited material classifies its transmission risk as uncertain, so unnecessary disconnections should be minimized and current infection-control guidance followed.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: Which three procedures are considered aerosol-generating surgical or procedural activities? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Upper-airway surgery, high-speed powered instrumentation, and upper-GI endoscopy can each generate aerosols or provoke respiratory-particle dispersion. The magnitude and infectious risk vary with the procedure and pathogen.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice

questions.stem: A department improves N95 use during AGPs. Which APSF safety priority is most directly supported?
questions.explanation: Respirator use during indicated aerosol-generating procedures is a barrier against occupational exposure and microbial transmission. Improving correct selection, fit testing, and use therefore supports the infection-prevention safety priority.
questions.sourceTitle: Miscellaneous Topics in Nurse Anesthesia Practice
